cases.candidate_script:
set -u
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/dnssec-keytag-collision-peer.py
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" prep || exit 98
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" serve 127.0.0.2 5340 ready 2> "$HOME/anchor-peer.err" & peer=$!
trap 'kill "$peer" 2>/dev/null; wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" waitudp 127.0.0.2 5340 || exit 98
control=$(/usr/bin/python3 "$H" control 127.0.0.2 5340 collision) || exit 98
[[ $control == control-ok ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$control"; exit 98; }
echo control-ok
export PATH="$HOME/pbin" BASHDNS_SERVER_PORT=5340 BASHDNS_TRUST_ANCHOR="$PWD/anchor.ds" BASHDNS_0X20=0
if dns query collision.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 3000 --validate > "$HOME/collision.out" 2> "$HOME/collision.err"; then echo collision=accepted; else echo collision=rejected; exit 1; fi
cases.purpose: DNSKEY key tags can collide; the first nonverifying matching key must not hide a later valid authenticated signing key.
cases.oracle: Independent BIND delv validates the deterministic signed chain containing two distinct DNSKEYs with the same algorithm and key tag before the candidate is queried.
cases.comparison: Reference accepts the chain and the candidate accepts the correct leaf signature; setup or reference failure fails the case.
